jobs.description:
Director of Operations

Company:
Happy Ice
Location:
Los Angeles and Anaheim, California
Reports To:
CEO and Founder
Position:
Full Time, Exempt
Salary Range:
$115,000 to $135,000, plus performance bonus
About Happy Ice

Happy Ice is a fast growing, Los Angeles born frozen dessert brand known for our artisanal take on Philadelphia Water Ice, Italian ice, soft serve, and unforgettable guest experiences. We have been recognized as one of the best frozen dessert destinations in Los Angeles and have built a brand that is loved by our community and known for bringing happiness wherever we go. One of our biggest milestones to date is being selected to operate inside Disneyland Resort, an incredible opportunity that represents how far the brand has come and where we believe it can go. Today, Happy Ice operates two brick and mortar locations, our Disneyland kiosk, two food trucks, and a full catering and events department. But we are just getting started.

Over the next 24 months, our goal is to open two additional locations and build the systems necessary to prepare Happy Ice for franchising.

We are looking for a Director of Operations who can help us build a profitable, efficient, trainable, and easily duplicatable business capable of taking Happy Ice nationwide.

Who We're Looking For

If your experience is primarily managing systems that were already built for you, please do not apply. We are looking for a builder and relentless executor who has developed operating systems, training programs, procedures, and processes. You should be able to take an operation and make it clear, measurable, teachable, profitable, and easily duplicatable. We are not hiring someone to manage the playbook. We are hiring someone to help build it.

Position Summary

The Director of Operations will lead Happy Ice's current operations while building the systems needed for our next stage of growth. This person will own profitability, P&Ls, people, systems, training, operational excellence, and franchise readiness. Our goal is to define how a great Happy Ice location operates down to a science.

Key Responsibilities

P&L and Profitability

Own the financial performance of our stores and operating departments.
Establish the KPIs that drive the Happy Ice economic engine and build clear scorecards around them.
Improve revenue, labor, food cost, controllable expenses, margins, and operating profit.
Build highly profitable locations with strong, repeatable unit economics.

Build the Happy Ice Operating System

Build and document the systems required to operate Happy Ice consistently and profitably.
Create clear standards for every critical area of the business, including service, production, cleaning, inventory, labor, and daily operations.
Build role specific training manuals and certification standards for every position.
Develop manager training and a train the trainer program.
Ensure every system is simple, teachable, measurable, and repeatable.
Improve staffing, labor productivity, production flow, service speed, store layout, employee movement, equipment placement, and customer flow.
Build an operating model that maximizes productivity without sacrificing quality or hospitality.

Leadership and Culture

Lead and develop Store Leaders and department managers.
Build strong systems for accountability, communication, performance management, and leadership development.
Turn Happy Ice's culture into clear behaviors, standards, training, and leadership systems that can be taught and duplicated across every future location.

Growth and Franchise Readiness

Help successfully open two additional Happy Ice locations within the next 24 months.
Prepare the company operationally for franchising.
Build a repeatable new store opening process.
Build an operating model that future franchise owners can successfully duplicate.

Qualifications

Strong multi unit restaurant or hospitality leadership experience.
Proven experience building operating systems, not simply managing them.
Strong P&L and financial management experience.
Experience improving labor, food cost, profitability, and productivity.
Experience developing SOPs, training systems, and leaders.
Experience opening new locations.
Strong attention to detail, organization, and project management skills.
Experience with growing brands or franchise systems is strongly preferred.
A relentless executor who sees what needs to be done, takes ownership, moves with urgency, obsesses over the details, and finishes what they start.

What Success Looks Like

Within 24 months, Happy Ice should have:

Developed Leader operating their locations with excellence.
Managers who understand and are accountable for their P&Ls.
Stronger and more predictable profitability.
Clearly defined KPIs that drive our economic engine.
Clear operating manuals and training systems.
Defined labor and productivity standards.
A complete training and certification program.
Two additional successfully opened locations.
A proven operating model ready for franchising.
A culture that has been translated into clear, teachable, and repeatable systems.

Our goal is to be able to hand a future franchise owner the Happy Ice operating system and confidently say: "This is how you operate a great Happy Ice location, and this is how you operate it profitably".

A Note From the CEO

Hello, Future World Changer.

You’ve already made an impact. You’ve experienced big wins, built great systems, and helped companies become better because you were there. You’ve worked alongside great leaders, gained valuable experience, and proven what you’re capable of. Now you’re looking for the big one. The opportunity to take everything you’ve learned and build something that dominates. This is it!

This is the opportunity where you won’t just be making a change, you’ll be making history. And you’ll feel great about it because of the impact we’ll make in our communities. The families, managers, team members, and franchisees around the world will all be positively impacted by what we create together.

Let’s have some fun, make history, and dominate the frozen dessert market nationally.
I look forward to speaking with you.

Lemeir Mitchell
Founder and CEO

Who We Are

Since opening in 1998, The Tech Interactive has been an integral part of the San Francisco Bay area and is proud to serve families and young people through hands-on activities, experimental labs, and design challenge experiences. 

Here at The Tech our mission is to inspire the innovator in everyone! We are a team of diverse individuals committed to creating learning experiences that empower young folks to innovate with creativity, curiosity, and compassion. We believe that technology is leading and transforming lives all over the world and we want to help develop the next generation of problem-solvers.

If you join our team, we know you will have a fulfilling and rewarding role focused on giving back to our community, especially those that have been historically marginalized and underserved. 

Position Overview

The Director of Major Gifts is a senior frontline fundraiser responsible for building meaningful relationships with individual donors and securing significant philanthropic support for The Tech Interactive’s mission and future.
This role manages a portfolio of major gift donors and prospects, with a strong emphasis on identifying and cultivating new supporters and regularly soliciting five- and six-figure gifts. The Director will develop individualized engagement and solicitation strategies, partner closely with organizational leadership, and help connect donors’ interests with The Tech’s programs, exhibits, community impact, and long-term vision.
The Director will also contribute to The Tech’s broader campaign efforts, helping develop donor strategies, case materials, and customized campaign proposals for significant prospects.
This exempt position reports to the Vice President of Development and works closely with the CEO.

Responsibilities 

Manage and grow a portfolio of major gift donors and prospects, leading relationships from identification and qualification through cultivation, solicitation, closing, and stewardship.
Regularly solicit five- and six-figure gifts and build a strong pipeline of new individual donors with the capacity and interest to make significant philanthropic investments.
Develop thoughtful, individualized strategies that connect donor interests with The Tech’s mission, programs, exhibits, community initiatives, and strategic priorities.
Build relationships through meaningful donor engagement, including one-on-one meetings, visits, events, and other opportunities to deepen connection to The Tech.
Partner with the Vice President of Development, CEO, individual gift officers, board members, and other organizational leaders on donor strategy, cultivation, and solicitation.
Support campaign fundraising by helping develop prospect strategies, compelling proposals, cases for support, and customized materials for major and principal gift opportunities.
Work with the Individual Gifts Officer and Donor Communications Manager to create effective cultivation and stewardship experiences for Leadership Circle and other major donors.
Maintain a strong understanding of The Tech’s programs, impact, and future plans and use donor and pipeline data to prioritize opportunities and drive results.

What You Bring

5+ years of progressively responsible fundraising experience, including demonstrated success managing relationships with individual major donors.
A track record of personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing five-figure gifts, with demonstrated experience or readiness to regularly solicit six-figure gifts.
Strong relationship-building instincts and the confidence to engage donors, board members, community leaders, and senior executives.
Experience developing donor strategies and managing a portfolio and pipeline toward ambitious fundraising goals.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to translate organizational priorities into compelling donor conversations and proposals.
Strong judgment, initiative, organization, and follow-through, with the ability to manage multiple sophisticated donor relationships simultaneously.
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.

Working Conditions and Schedule

This role is based at The Tech Interactive in downtown San Jose and requires a meaningful on-site presence because relationship building is central to the position. Some flexibility to work from an alternative location may be available depending on business needs and scheduled meetings.
The position also includes meetings with corporate partners throughout the Bay Area and occasional evening and weekend events.

To that end, we look for a diverse pool of applicants including but not limited to those from historically marginalized groups — women, people with disabilities, people of color, people who are lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and/or nonconforming, veterans, and people from different socioeconomic backgrounds.

jobs.description:
Executive Director/Producer of Superfair Art Fair - Full-Time w/ Flex Summers

About The Superfair

The Superfair is one of the US’ leading artist-first contemporary art fairs. We make the process of buying and selling art more accessible for artists and potential buyers. We’ve led our sector for 11 years and are planning major expansion over the next 2 years. With a growth target of 8 global cities by the end of F/Y 2028, we support independent artists through curated art fairs, professional development, and hands-on guidance. We focus on diversity in our visitor audiences and artist rosters, with an emphasis on women, the LGBTQ+ spectrum, and people of color.

Unlike an art gallery or other art fairs for artists, The Superfair takes no commission on art sold: our artists keep 100% of their income from sales. We operate on a client-provider model, similar to a trade show. 85% of our revenue is derived from booth sales, 10% from ticket sales, and 5% from sponsorship. There are opportunities to drive additional revenue from tickets, sponsors, and channel partnerships while maintaining a robust B2B stream from artist clients.

Our work blends large-scale event production, artist education, audience building, and programming to help artists build sustainable careers and introduce new audiences to contemporary art.

We are at an inflection point where competing within the market involves scaling the number of annual events and expanding to thoughtfully chosen new markets while providing a high standard of service to our core clients - artists - and fun, engaging events centered around buying and selling art. 

The Ideal Candidate

If you thrive wearing multiple hats, enjoy variety and travel in your work, and like to see ambitious ideas through to reality, we want to meet you!

This is a senior-level position for an exceptionally organized, proactive executive-level organization + project manager who can effectively balance operations management with creative, design-based thinking.

You will become the leadership team of The Superfair, and will coordinate every aspect of The Superfair’s events around the US.

As team leader, you will produce 2 high-production art fairs in FY 2026, 5 in FY 2027, and maintain a growth rate of 1-2 additional events per year. One of your first projects will be to assemble a support team around you. We will work together to create the guidelines of that team. It will be up to you to determine whether to retain this support team on a seasonal, fractional, or ongoing basis.

The ideal Executive Director is calm under pressure, naturally collaborative, highly empathetic, and energized by solving problems before they arise. You enjoy building systems, managing many moving pieces at once, and making both clients and teammates feel supported, while keeping the organization’s stakeholders and bottom line at front of mind.

Because of the number of stakeholders, this is a role for a systems-oriented thinker who is willing and capable of putting in front-end work early on to develop systems that allow for scaling to any number of clients and audience, without creating excess operational demands. 

You genuinely need to love artists and their work, and want to do everything you can to see them succeed.

You must understand how to use leverage to create scalable long-term solutions. Not simply trading hours of hard work for results, but developing and employing systems that make it easier for you and your team to execute top notch events over and over again.

Responsibilities

Project Management & Operations

Revamp existing databases of client information, using tools such as Claude and other AI and non-AI tools to increase efficiency, automate processes, and create scalable systems throughout the organization – including clean, workable spreadsheets with real-time output reporting. 

Lead budget management with Operations Manager by allocating resources and identifying creative, cost-effective solutions.

Maintain and present fiscally responsible event budgets along parameters set with Ownership at least 45 days prior to each event

Work with Operations Manager on contracts, rentals, vendor negotiation + coordination, signage plan, municipality and venue-level compliance - including liquor/F&B, fire + safety, and anything else related to a successful large scale event attended by thousands of people.

Track project timelines, budgets, and key deliverables for fairs, sponsorships, and partnerships.

Maintain and improve organizational systems, shared drives, and internal documentation + compliance.

Coordinate hiring and scheduling for temporary event staff.

Collaborate with Floor Plan Designer on event floor plans, artist layouts, signage placement, and visitor flow.

Spearhead ongoing planning meetings and cross-department collaboration.

Fair Production & On-Site Management

Serve as the primary on-site lead during installation and fair week ( **additional pay commensurate with additional hours worked )

Coordinate venue logistics and maintain strong relationships with venue partners.

Manage rentals including walls, furniture, AV, and production equipment.

Coordinate food & beverage vendors and hospitality needs (in tandem with Operations Manager)

Oversee artist load-in, installation schedules, and exhibitor support.

Delegate responsibilities to on-site staff and volunteers while maintaining a positive, solutions-oriented atmosphere.

Be the primary point of contact for artists throughout installation and event days.

Artist Relations & Curatorial Support

Our artist clients and their satisfaction is at the heart of our business. You are responsible for creating an experience where clients feel genuinely cared for.

You'll:

Develop SOPs and FAQs for addressing artist questions, utilizing existing resources and building upon them.

Create a broad guide for all fairs, and specific fair FAQs/logistical plans for each, building on existing resources.

Respond to client emails and questions promptly and professionally (or ensure that a support team member can do so, and that timelines for response are clearly communicated.)

Provide clear timelines, deadlines, and logistical information.

Review booth layouts and offer thoughtful curatorial feedback to clients (Ownership and volunteer/part-time programmers may assist)

Assist clients with exhibition planning and presentation.

Support clients through the inevitable excitement and anxieties that come with exhibiting their work.

Creative Collaboration

This role goes beyond logistics. A penchant for design thinking and creativity is critical to your success and the fair’s ongoing ability to compete and innovate in the marketplace

You'll work with Ownership and other teams to implement:

Public programming and interactive experiences.

Artist education initiatives.

Marketing campaigns and promotional ideas.

Ways to improve the overall artist and visitor experience.

New opportunities that strengthen The Superfair's mission and community.

We're looking for someone who is passionate about the role of the art fair in a thriving, sustainable art market, and is excited to help shape its future – not just execute a checklist.

Qualifications

We recognize that exceptional leaders come from many backgrounds. If you've successfully led complex live productions or mission-driven organizations - even outside the art space - we encourage you to apply.

Ideal candidates will have:

5+ years of senior-level project management or event coordination experience (backgrounds in art fairs, live events, theater, weddings, festivals, or similar fields are all welcome).

High comfort level making thoughtful decisions, often with incomplete information.

Exceptional + demonstrable project management skills.

Graduate level, empathetic written and verbal communication.

Expert level knowledge and hands-on experience with spreadsheets, CRMs, and project management tools.

The ability to remain calm, organized, and solution-oriented under pressure.
Strong attention to detail and follow-through.

Excellent interpersonal skills with a warm, empathetic approach to working with artists.

A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for brainstorming new ideas.

A genuine passion for contemporary art and supporting independent artists.

This may not be the role for you if:

You prefer and have only worked in highly structured corporate environments. You will set the pace, structure, and set + meet your own goals within the role, in tandem with ownership.

You can’t or don’t like to travel. You will need to travel to each fair for production, and possibly conduct shorter site and cultural visits during the run up to each.

You expect to inherit clean systems rather than build ones that are usable team-wide, but also suited to your own style and preferences.

You see operations and creativity as separate disciplines – in this role, they are part and parcel to success.

Why Lead The Superfair?

This is a rare opportunity to shape one of the country's leading artist-first art fairs. We are a legacy business with 11 years of history, hundreds of thousands of visitors, and 40+ fairs under our belt. We are hitting our stride where city selection and team building are concerned, and recognize the challenges facing the overall art fair landscape.

You'll collaborate directly with Ownership on big picture planning, make meaningful creative decisions, and play an essential role in building events that put artists and audiences first. Every fair is different, every project presents new challenges, and every season offers opportunities to create memorable experiences for artists and audiences alike.

With the right leader in this role, the sky is the limit as far as growth and expansion, and we’re eager to begin that journey with you.

ED Compensation - starting between $85,000 and $105,000 annually + $600/month healthcare contribution. Initial compensation commensurate with experience.

There is significant opportunity for advancement as the organization expands nationally and globally over the next 1 to 3 years.

Overview

The earliest years of a child’s life create the foundation for lifelong health, learning, and emotional well-being. At Brookdale Hospital, the HealthySteps Program Director has the opportunity to shape that foundation by leading an innovative, evidence-based program that integrates child development and infant mental health expertise directly into pediatric primary care.

The Program Director provides the strategic, clinical, administrative, and operational leadership necessary to ensure that infants, young children, and their families receive coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate support in pediatric primary care. The Program Director leads a multidisciplinary team and oversees program quality and fidelity, staff development, grant administration, fiscal performance, clinical operations, data and outcomes reporting, and community partnerships.

HealthySteps, a nationally recognized program of ZERO TO THREE, strengthens the traditional pediatric care model by addressing the developmental, behavioral, social-emotional, and family needs that influence a child’s ability to thrive. HealthySteps at Brookdale Hospital is supported by public and private funding and participates in a multisite, statewide initiative funded by the New York State Office of Mental Health to expand and integrate mental health services within pediatric primary care.

Through collaborative leadership and a commitment to health equity, the Program Director advances Brookdale Hospital’s ability to give children and families—particularly those from historically under-served communities—the strongest possible start in life.

This is a full-time, office-based position in the Washington, DC area, with approximately 50% travel and additional travel as required for the role.

Reports to: the Board of Relief International USA, working closely with the Relief International Network Leadership Team.

Salary range: US$170,000 to US$180,000 per annum plus performance bonus and benefits.

Contract: Permanent, full-time.

This role is classified as requiring enhanced pre-employment checks.

About Relief International

Relief International (RI) is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. We work in 16 countries across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, providing Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience.

About the Opportunity

This senior leadership role manages the Relief International US entity. Reporting to the Board of Relief International USA, you will build and deliver the strategy that grows and diversifies our US donor base and oversee US grants.
Your first priority is to build a strong and varied pipeline of US income across philanthropy, institutional donors and the private sector, and to turn it into reliable, flexible funding. You will also oversee all US grants, hold legal and fiduciary responsibility for the US entity, and represent Relief International to US policymakers and partners.
As an experienced fundraising leader with a creative, entrepreneurial approach, you will open new doors with major donors, foundations, corporate partners and institutional funders, while also leading advocacy and policy engagement with US government stakeholders. You will work closely with the Executive Director for France and the United Kingdom, the Resource Development, Technical and Programme Implementation (PID) Directors, and the Boards, to ensure alignment across the Network.

Your Responsibilities

This role includes the following responsibilities:
Provide day-to-day and strategic management of the US entity, including oversight of compliance with all relevant laws, data and RI Network policies in the US.
Lead all fundraising in the US, across individual giving, foundations, corporate partners and institutional donors, and build the team, systems and data needed to sustain growth.
Hold and grow a personal portfolio of major donor, foundation and corporate relationships, closing significant gifts and running fundraising events that meet agreed income goals.
Build Relief International's standing with US institutional funders, shaping a competitive bid pipeline with Network technical and programme teams, and strengthening our position in consortia and partnerships.
Report to the Board on income against target, the strength of the pipeline, donor retention and the return on what we invest in fundraising.
Develop and lead RI US advocacy and policy engagement with US government stakeholders, including Congressional offices, multilateral institutions and advocacy coalitions.
Work with the global Communications Team to hone RI’s brand identity, secure media exposure and raise the organizational profile with the US audiences that matter most to fundraising and influence.
Oversee all US grants awarded to the US entity, holding accountability for donor compliance across the whole portfolio, and monitor the performance of services provided by the network.
Act as the main point of contact for US grant donors from award through to close-out.
Hold legal, fiduciary and regulatory responsibility for the US entity, including 501(c)(3) obligations, IRS filings, state charitable registrations, the annual audit and applicable US government grant regulations, and serve as its senior officer, accountable to the Board.
Lead, develop and retain the US team, upholding RI’s safeguarding commitments and sustaining a positive, productive work environment free from harassment and bullying.

What You Bring

You will bring the following experience and skills.
A minimum of 12 to 15 years of substantial proven experience in a senior leadership role within an international non-profit, humanitarian or development organization, with accountability for entity management, budget oversight and revenue growth. Experience should include at least five years at director level or above.
A strong personal track record of securing significant income across US major gifts, foundations, corporate partnerships and institutional donors, with clear evidence of the scale of gifts closed.
Experience of leading revenue diversification, including reducing dependence on a narrow institutional funding base and growing unrestricted income.
Sound working knowledge of US non-profit governance and compliance, including 501(c)(3) obligations, and proven experience of overseeing US government grants, including their audit and reporting requirements.
Demonstrated experience of advocacy and policy engagement with US government stakeholders, including Congressional offices and humanitarian coordination forums.
Experience working effectively with a Board, including on strategy, risk and income performance, and of collaborating across a multi-entity or federated network structure.
Excellent communications and representation skills, with the ability to act as a credible spokesperson at conferences, roundtables and high-level stakeholder engagements.
Knowledge of donor requirements for safeguarding standards and protection from sexual exploitation and abuse.
Demonstrated sensitivity to diversity, equity, inclusion, cultural difference and gender issues, and a strong commitment to RI’s values.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

We are proud to be a global recruiter, hiring people from around the world. We offer competitive salaries and benefit packages for all staff, that are applied fairly and transparently.

Note you must have the existing right to work in the United States.

Relief International is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by federal, state or local law, and we provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities at every stage of recruitment.

If you’re excited about this role, but your experience doesn’t align with every criteria described, we encourage you to apply anyway, you could be exactly what we need!

To apply for this post, click on the “ Apply

You will be asked to upload a CV and Cover Letter
.

ABOUT ARCH GRANTS

Arch Grants has been disrupting the status quo in economic development since its inception with a mission to transform the Saint Louis economy – attracting and retaining extraordinary entrepreneurs, one cohort at a time. As a 501(c)(3), Arch Grants is passionate about accelerating place-based economic development via equity-free startup funding. Best known for its global Startup Competition, Arch Grants has now funded 291 companies that have gone on to create 4,000+ jobs, commercialize 7,000+ products, land 300+ patents, attract $894M+ in capital raised, and generate $1.3B+ in revenue.

In addition to non-dilutive cash awards, Arch Grants offers unparalleled resources and structured support, aimed at multiplying the success of its early-stage startups by driving capital, credibility and strategic introductions. Be it connections to accelerator programs, venture capital firms, angel investors, mentors, Arch Grants programming, or even local enterprise customers, the data has shown the majority of founders choose to stay, hire, and reinvest in Saint Louis.

Beyond its startup success stories, Arch Grants has not only proven that the maturation of an ecosystem where bold ideas take root, scale rapidly, and attract national attention is possible, but also stepped into close collaboration with key ecosystem partners, including local chambers, major universities, ag-tech and geospatial hubs, and other community conveners to attract and retain high-growth startups, high-potential talent, and business opportunity to Saint Louis.

In alignment with its next set of strategic and financial goals, Arch Grants is excited to announce its need for a Chief Executive Officer.
As Arch Grants’ first-ever CEO, you will help define this role and shape the organization’s next chapter: a rare opportunity to build rather than inherit. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO will provide focused strategic leadership across operations, fund development and organizational growth. Leading a talented team of 8-10 internal employees and an annual operating budget of approximately $3.6 million, with an endowment and investment portfolio of approximately $23 million, Arch Grants’ CEO will safeguard the organization’s mission, align ambitious programming with internal capacity, and maintain operational and financial stability. The CEO will also elevate Arch Grants’ national profile by cultivating donors and strategic partners, diversifying funding sources, and securing multi-year financial commitments that support long-term sustainability. Learn more at www.archgrants.org.

YOUR MISSION AS CEO

• EXECUTIVE LEADERSHIP + MISSION STEWARDSHIP – In close partnership with the Arch Grants Board of Directors, you will drive executive leadership and organizational insight to inform strategic decision making. You will translate strategy into actionable goals and lead focused and accountable execution. You will protect against mission creep, ensuring new programs align with organizational purpose, capabilities and desired impact. You will facilitate Board engagement through timely, transparent communications on all strategic, financial and fiduciary matters.

• FUND DEVELOPMENT + FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY – As a driving force behind the organization’s financial sustainability, you will lead and align key staff, Board members, and stakeholders around a comprehensive development strategy. You will expand and diversify the funding base, encompassing stewardship of major gifts, foundation and corporate relations, planned giving, strategic partners and advancement operations to secure multi-year commitments and endowment growth. Own full P&L responsibility, including budget, forecasting, cash flow, and financial controls to ensure Arch Grants is positioned for desired impact.

• TEAM LEADERSHIP + OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE – Lead, develop and align a talented internal team, ensuring a culture of collaboration, accountability, and recognition. Own the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of Arch Grants’ programs, scaled to capacity and aligned with organizational mission. Own internal ops, technology, data, systems, and all third-party partners to support execution, decision making, and growth.

• NATIONAL PROFILE: PARTNERSHIPS & EXTERNAL RELATIONS – Serving as chief ambassador, you will elevate brand and visibility, positioning Arch Grants as a national voice on entrepreneurship, economic development and founder attraction. Cultivate meaningful relationships with community and civic leaders, venture networks, corporate partners, and ecosystem colleagues. Serve as the public face of the organization, representing Arch
Grants to increase awareness of its model, impact, and role in attracting entrepreneurs and early-stage business to Saint Louis.

• IMPACT + GROWTH – Track economic and community impact through measurement of metrics that matter, reflecting Arch Grants’ role as a catalyst in economic transformation through entrepreneurship and regional retention. Oversee annual reporting, multi-year cohort tracking, founder feedback, and periodic third-party economic impact analysis.

IS THIS A MATCH FOR YOU?

• You have a passion for the mission of Arch Grants, including a fundamental belief in the power of an entrepreneurial ecosystem to foster economic growth. You consider yourself a builder of process, products, and people and fundraising strategist who thrives on making the next chapter of an organization’s vision come to life.

• You have gained 10-15+ years of progressive senior leadership experience spanning strategy, operations, and resource development, and management of people, processes, programs, and organizational resources. Experience must include no less than 5 years of direct team oversight, including an ability to inspire and motivate, manage conflict, and foster a healthy organizational culture.

• You bring a proven track record in leading transformational fund development initiatives, including an ability to secure multi-year gifts and the strategy to diversify fund sources. Equivalent experience leading strategic growth initiatives in an entrepreneurial, venture, or economic-development context is also welcome. Prior experience managing high-level donors and prospects capable of six- and seven-figure gifts is required. Development of strategic partnerships, foundation and corporate relations, and grant funding also desired. Evidence of a data-driven approach to fundraising a must-have.

• You are well-versed in proactively communicating with internal and external stakeholders. You confidently interact with team at all levels and react with diplomacy and tact. You bring experience communicating a vision and prospective road map to key stakeholders and community constituents. Ability to build bridges between like- minded organizations to foster collaboration, drive open communication and cooperative partnerships desired.

• You are willing to serve as a hands-on leader, with the ability and desire to flex between strategic and tactical priorities. Superior project management skills, an ability to support organization-wide strategic planning efforts, and a bold, proactive mindset are required.

• You are committed to building an inclusive organizational culture and believe that attracting a wide range of talented entrepreneurs and organizational stakeholders will further our success.

• You have developed a solid business acumen, prior P&L responsibility and strong technology skills. Four- year college degree required or equivalent executive leadership experience. MBA or graduate degree, a plus.

WHY JOIN US?

• MAKE A FOREVER IMPACT IN SAINT LOUIS – Become part of a mission that is changing the economic reality and community landscape in the Saint Louis region. Build the leadership fabric of tomorrow in the Saint Louis community.

• WE ARE EVOLVING AS AN ORGANIZATION – As an organization, evolution is at our core. We believe it is critical to achieving our ongoing strategic and economic development goals. We are seeking a leader with a shared vision, along with the drive and fundraising expertise to support Arch Grants on its journey to a next set of critical milestones.

WORK LOCATION + TRAVEL + RELOCATION

This position requires a consistent in-person presence at our primary office location in Saint Louis, Missouri. Ability and willingness to attend evening events and to travel as needed on a limited basis is required. Travel outside the local area is estimated at 10%. Relocation stipend available and immediate relocation will be desired.

COMPENSATION PACKAGE

The CEO position offers a competitive compensation package, including a base salary commensurate with experience in the range of $190,000.00 to approximately $300,000.00, along with a comprehensive benefits package, including: medical, dental, vision, life, accident, STD, LTD, paid time off, professional development, and retirement plan with match. Placement within the compensation range will reflect the selected candidate’s experience and qualifications and the Board's compensation benchmarking.

TO APPLY

Apply via LinkedIn or online at www.occhiosearch.com.

We ask that you direct all questions, candidate referrals, and applications to our retained search consultants at Occhio Search & Recruitment. All inquiries held in strict confidence. Arch Grants is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for all applicants. If you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please let us know. For questions, contact sarah@occhiosearch.com, angie@occhiosearch.com, or elly@occhiosearch.com.

Arch Grants is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome differences in form of gender, race, ancestry, ethnicity, disability, socioeconomic status, age, political affiliation, marital status, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, and veteran status. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and we look forward to hearing
from you!

Overview

The Tufts University School of Medicine is launching the Sam W. Ho Center for Health Care Transformation (Ho Center, the Center), a new multidisciplinary center dedicated to advancing health care innovation, improving population health, and achieving health justice. The Center will bring together faculty, researchers, clinicians, students, and external partners across Tufts University, Tufts Medicine, and other health care systems to develop transformative solutions to today's most pressing health challenges.

The Center will serve as a hub for collaboration across medicine, public health, allied health, community health, economics, informatics, nutritional sciences, veterinary medicine, dental medicine, policy, and communications. Through this cross-disciplinary approach, the Center will identify research, educational, and clinical priorities that advance health care transformation, improve health outcomes, and promote evidence-based solutions to today's most pressing health challenges. Areas of focus may include health justice, climate justice, food as medicine, community health, housing justice, and digital health.

Established through the philanthropy and vision of Tufts trustee and alumnus Dr. Sam W. Ho, the Center reflects his lifelong commitment to advancing health justice and transforming health care delivery.

Reporting initially to the Dean of Tufts University School of Medicine, the Executive Director will play a pivotal leadership role in building and growing the Center. Working closely with the Dean, Center leadership, and faculty across the School of Medicine and Tufts University, the Executive Director will help shape and advance the Center's research, education, and policy agenda while providing strategic, operational, and organizational leadership. This is a unique opportunity for a visionary and entrepreneurial leader to help establish a newly launched center with the potential to influence health care transformation at local, national, and global levels.

This is a fully onsite leadership position based at Tufts University's Health Sciences campus in Boston. Regular on-campus presence is expected five days per week.

What You'll Do

As Executive Director, you will provide strategic, operational, and organizational leadership to support the successful launch, development, growth, and long-term sustainability of the Sam W. Ho Center for Health Care Transformation. Working closely with the Dean, Center leadership, faculty, and stakeholders across academic, clinical, industry, governmental, philanthropic, and community sectors, you will help establish the Center and advance its mission through research, education, policy, and health care transformation initiatives.

Responsibilities include:

Lead Strategic Planning and Growth

Partner with Center leadership to develop, implement, and monitor the Center's strategic vision and long-range goals, providing regular updates and recommendations to leadership.
Help shape future directions for research, education, policy, and health care transformation initiatives.
Identify opportunities to expand the Center's impact across Tufts University and through external partnerships.

Direct Operations and Financial Management

Oversee the day-to-day operations of the Center and ensure successful execution of priorities, programs, and initiatives.
Manage budgets, resources, and operational planning in collaboration with Center and School of Medicine leadership.
Develop operational policies, processes, and infrastructure that support organizational effectiveness and ensure successful implementation of the Center's strategic priorities and future growth.
Recruit, manage, and support staff while fostering accountability and collaboration across Center activities.

Advance Funding and External Partnerships

Identify, cultivate, and secure funding opportunities through government agencies, foundations, industry partners, philanthropy, and other external sources.
Lead and support grant development efforts that expand the Center's research, education, and policy portfolio.
Build and maintain strategic relationships with academic institutions, health systems, industry leaders, and funding partners.
Advance business development, marketing, and public engagement efforts that elevate the Center's visibility, impact, and external partnerships.

Drive Collaboration and Program Success

Oversee a portfolio of multidisciplinary research, education, and policy initiatives, ensuring progress toward key milestones and objectives.
Foster collaboration among faculty, researchers, clinicians, administrators, students, and external partners to advance the Center's mission.
Develop a strong understanding of the scientific, research, and educational priorities driving the Center's mission and use that knowledge to inform strategic planning, resource allocation, decision-making, and program development.
Stay informed about emerging scientific, educational, and industry developments, identifying opportunities for innovation, growth, and new collaborations.

Serve as a Representative for the Center

Act as an ambassador and public representative for the Center, communicating its mission, initiatives, and impact to internal and external audiences through presentations, media engagement, and other speaking opportunities.

What We're Looking For

To receive full consideration, applicants should apply online and include

Current resume/CV
Cover letter (maximum two pages) addressing the following:

Leadership, Strategy, and Organizational Impact

Please describe how your experience has prepared you to lead a multidisciplinary center, organization, or initiative. Highlight examples of strategic leadership, partnership development, organizational growth, and, where applicable, experience securing external funding. We are particularly interested in how you have translated organizational, scientific, research, educational, or policy priorities into impactful programs, operations, or initiatives.

Basic Requirements

Knowledge and experience typically acquired by:

MD and/or PhD in a health science discipline.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in academic medicine, health care, research administration, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading an academic research center, consortium, major healthcare initiative, or serving in a senior healthcare industry leadership role.

About Our Job

Situated approximately 24 miles northeast of downtown Denver, DEN is the primary air carrier airport serving the region. According to Airports Council International, in 2025, DEN was the fourth busiest airport in the United States and the tenth busiest in the world, serving 82.4 million annual passengers. DEN spans across a 53-square-mile campus, an area twice the size of the island of Manhattan and is the second largest physical airport in the world. The passenger terminal complex is reached via Peña Boulevard, a 12-mile dedicated access road which connects Interstate 70 and intersects with the E-470 toll highway. DEN has six runways—four oriented north-south and two oriented east-west. Five runways are 12,000 feet long and 150 feet wide. The sixth runway is 16,000 feet long and 200 feet wide, providing unrestricted global access for any airline and the ability to accommodate fully loaded jumbo jets, including the Airbus A-380. DEN is a major hub for United, Southwest, and Frontier Airlines, currently supporting more than 43,000 badged employees, 25 commercial airlines, 236 nonstop destinations, and generates an annual economic impact of more than $47 billion for Colorado.

The city is seeking a driven, dynamic, results-oriented leader who will employ strategic and tactical leadership to ensure that DEN remains a strong economic engine for the region, while providing safe and efficient facilities and superior services and amenities to airline, passengers, concessionaires, and other airport stakeholders.

The Director oversees all daily operations, manages program curriculum, supervises CDL Instructors, Examiners, and the Program Manager, and serves as the primary liaison to state/federal regulatory agencies, industry employers, and community partners. Additionally, the Director obtains and maintains New Mexico DMV CDL Examiner certification, provides direct classroom and behind-the-wheel instruction, oversees state testing operations, and collaborates closely with the CTE/Workforce Development Director on grant opportunities, strategic partnerships, and statewide workforce initiatives.

Departmental Operations & Strategic Leadership

Provides administrative and operational oversight for all CDL, Heavy Equipment, and related workforce development programs.
Ensures smooth program execution across main, satellite, and mobile training locations.
Manages program courses, schedules, and administrative workflows within the Modern Campus management system.

Supervision & Personnel Management

Leads recruitment, hiring, onboarding, professional development, and performance reviews for departmental staff.

Regulatory Compliance & Agency Reporting

Compiles, verifies, and submits required compliance and performance reports to state and federal agencies.

Curriculum & Assessment Development

Leads the continuous development, evaluation, and modernization of CDL and Heavy Equipment curricula, incorporating state-of-the-art simulator technologies and hands-on fieldwork standards.
Oversees student learning outcome assessments to ensure workforce readiness.

Testing Guidance & Examiner Certification

Provides guidance, quality control, and direct oversight of all institutional CDL skills testing operations, ensuring LCC’s status as a compliant stationary and mobile testing facility.

Advanced knowledge of adult learning theories, curriculum design, classroom instruction, simulator training, and field evaluation methods.
Demonstrated leadership, supervisory, coaching, and conflict-resolution skills.
Proficiency in operating Class A commercial vehicles and various types of heavy equipment.
Strong organizational, administrative, and project management skills with systems like Modern Campus.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for presenting to state agencies, industry partners, and executive leadership.
Ability to analyze workforce data, write grant proposals, and manage program budgets effectively.
Ability to work effectively with diverse student, employee, and community populations.

Required

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND LICENSES

Examiner Status: Must possess or be eligible to immediately obtain and maintain New Mexico DMV CDL Examiner Certification.
Field & Teaching Experience: Minimum of five (5) years of combined professional experience in commercial driving/heavy equipment operation and instructional delivery in CDL or heavy equipment training programs.
Supervisory Experience: Minimum of two (2) years of supervisory, lead, or administrative management experience overseeing personnel, program operations, or safety compliance within a CDL, fleet, or technical education environment.
Mobility: Valid NM driver's license and ability to travel as required by the institution.

The earliest years of a child’s life create the foundation for lifelong health, learning, and emotional well-being. At Brookdale Hospital, the HealthySteps Program Director has the opportunity to shape that foundation by leading an innovative, evidence-based program that integrates child development and infant mental health expertise directly into pediatric primary care.

The Program Director provides the strategic, clinical, administrative, and operational leadership necessary to ensure that infants, young children, and their families receive coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate support in pediatric primary care. The Program Director leads a multidisciplinary team and oversees program quality and fidelity, staff development, grant administration, fiscal performance, clinical operations, data and outcomes reporting, and community partnerships.

HealthySteps, a nationally recognized program of ZERO TO THREE, strengthens the traditional pediatric care model by addressing the developmental, behavioral, social-emotional, and family needs that influence a child’s ability to thrive. HealthySteps at Brookdale Hospital is supported by public and private funding and participates in a multisite, statewide initiative funded by the New York State Office of Mental Health to expand and integrate mental health services within pediatric primary care.
